title: Overproduction makes a struggle for existence inevitable

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Overproduction makes a struggle for existence inevitable

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because all organisms tend to increase at a high (geometrical) rate, more individuals are produced than can survive, so every species must undergo a struggle for existence with members of its own species, with other species, or with physical conditions.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: A struggle for existence inevitably follows from the high rate at which all organic beings tend to increase.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter III, “Struggle for Existence”; section “Geometrical powers of increase”. Scope: all plants and animals in a state of nature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch03-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Demographic matrices directly estimate growth potential and realized limitation across many plants and animals. The universal wording exceeds coverage, but the central mechanism has clear and broadly testable consequences.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare potential population growth from fecundity and survival schedules with observed long-run abundance, and quantify density-, enemy- or environment-dependent mortality. Potential production exceeding realized recruitment with limiting mortality supports the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Struggle' requires mapping to measurable density dependence or mortality.

Microbes and many invertebrates are underrepresented.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.84
data existence: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open matrix-population and abundance databases can test geometrical potential versus realized numbers for hundreds of species, and the calculation is standard. The universal scope is only sampled, and the tripartite 'struggle' is hard to refute because every limit falls into one of the three bins. The resolvable part is overproduction, not the exhaustive classification of checks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare potential population growth at low density, from fecundity and survival schedules, with realized long-term abundance. Potential growth well above replacement, with realized numbers checked by conspecifics, other species, or physical factors, would support the argument; life histories whose maximum growth is at or below replacement would refute universal geometrical overproduction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The struggle is said to be with conspecifics, other species, or physical conditions, a disjunction that covers every possible check.

Potential growth estimated from a short study can misrepresent the long-run tendency to increase.

Demographic matrices are biased toward plants, vertebrates, and temperate studies.

discriminating power: 0.44
operationalizability: 0.66
